threshold_selection.note: Every alternative threshold is selected on validation rows only; cold/demo figures are reported, not used.

pick_threshold_tie_mechanism.reading: recall_at_precision() walks rows one by one in score order and stops inside the tied block of rows where cumulative precision is still >= 0.5; applying `score >= threshold` then flags the whole tied block, so the realised validation precision falls below the 0.5 target. Sigmoid calibration (the champion) has no ties, so its realised precision met the target.

cold_ledger_end_counterfactual_attributi.reading: Attribution diagnostic only (not a model): the margin minus one feature group's TreeSHAP contribution, calibrated and thresholded as deployed.

label_correction_effect.reading: Ordinary accounts are negatives under both label sets, so their flag rate cannot move with the label correction; only the FPR denominator and the unmaterialised-role rows change.

champion.rows: ledger-end snapshot only, old planned-role labels

as_reported.reading: The two reported gaps are measured on different rows (one snapshot vs four pooled snapshots, prevalence 7.4% vs 3.6%) and different labels, so they are not directly comparable.

like_for_like_current_labels.note: Current labels on identical rows. The champion was fitted on the ledger-end train rows only (with the old labels); earlier snapshots of train accounts were never in its fit.

refits_train_split_only_analysis.note: Raw (uncalibrated) scores. Folds keep scenario instances together (modeling.group_folds). Validation is reported, never used to choose anything here.

a_long_history_false_positives.not_cold_specific: Validation already shows it: ledger-end FPR champion 0.0853 vs challenger 0.1158; cold 0.0937 vs 0.116. Validation and cold feature distributions of ordinary accounts at the ledger end are close (ordinary_feature_means_by_as_of_day). The promotion rule did not look at long-history FPR.
a_long_history_false_positives.H1_pooled_threshold_dominated_by_short_h: Pooled validation rows are split evenly across history bands (shares [0.2465, 0.2584, 0.2524, 0.2428]). Re-selecting with the same rule on validation ledger-end rows only gives the same threshold (0.057471), because of H2.
a_long_history_false_positives.H2_isotonic_step_at_threshold: supported: The threshold equals the isotonic plateau for raw scores [0.035012, 0.100033]. On cold at the ledger end 416 of 1189 flags lie on that plateau: 397 of the 718 false positives, at plateau precision 0.0457. pick_threshold()/recall_at_precision() stops inside the tied block, so the realised pooled-validation precision at the deployed threshold is 0.3906, not >= 0.5. Analysis only (chosen on validation): a tie-aware threshold (0.068966) gives cold ledger-end FPR 0.0517 / recall 0.8777 (champion 0.0937 / 0.9068); the same rule on raw scores (0.082242) gives 0.0606 / 0.8874; matched to the champion's validation ledger-end FPR (raw) gives 0.0784 / 0.8913.
a_long_history_false_positives.H3_features_drift_with_history: supporte: Cold FPR by as_of day ['as_of_day_30', 'as_of_day_60', 'as_of_day_90', 'ledger_end_day_120']: champion [0.3154, 0.1742, 0.1055, 0.0937], challenger [0.0098, 0.0505, 0.0806, 0.116]. For ordinary accounts the challenger's mean TreeSHAP contribution moves from day 30 to day 120: behaviour -7.015 -> -4.076, graph -1.849 -> -0.689, account age 0.075 -> -0.104 (log-odds). Long-history false positives that only the challenger flags carry graph contribution 0.286 vs -0.724 for long-history true negatives, led by sender_forwarders_share. Removing the graph contribution would raise the cold ledger-end FPR to 0.1424 and removing the account-age contribution to 0.1246 (as scored 0.116): neither feature group adds false positives overall. Even with the tie-aware threshold the challenger's cold FPR still rises with history ({'<30 days': 0.0063, '30-60 days': 0.0212, '60-90 days': 0.0401, '>=90 days': 0.053}).
a_long_history_false_positives.H4_label_correction: not a cause: Ordinary accounts are negatives under both label sets; ordinary flag rates are identical under old and current labels (challenger 0.1198, champion 0.0947). Cold ledger-end FPR under old labels: champion 0.0915, challenger 0.1157.

b_train_validation_gap.reported_gaps_are_not_like_for_like: The two reported gaps are measured on different rows (one snapshot vs four pooled snapshots, prevalence 7.4% vs 3.6%) and different labels, so they are not directly comparable.
b_train_validation_gap.like_for_like_ledger_end_current_labels: champion 0.1164 vs challenger 0.1244; pooled snapshots champion 0.101 vs challenger 0.1586. The challenger's train PR-AUC is ~1.0 at every as_of day; its validation PR-AUC is lowest at day 30 (0.6518), which is what widens the pooled gap.
b_train_validation_gap.H_min_child_weight_1_with_near_duplicate: 0 of 21073 consecutive snapshot pairs are identical (63 identical apart from account age). min_child_weight=5 changes in-sample/out-of-fold PR-AUC from 0.9998/0.8694 to 0.9996/0.869; one snapshot per account: in-sample 1.0, and the frozen challenger's train PR-AUC on one snapshot per account is 0.9994.
b_train_validation_gap.what_the_gap_is: In-sample saturation of 624 depth-4 trees, not leakage: group 5-fold out-of-fold PR-AUC inside train is 0.8694, close to validation 0.8473 (raw scores). The champion's configuration refitted on current labels shows the same pattern (0.1261 in-sample minus out-of-fold). Isotonic ties also cost pooled validation PR-AUC 0.8473 (raw) -> 0.8407 (calibrated).
b_train_validation_gap.learning_curve: validation PR-AUC (pooled) by share of train groups: 0.25: 0.7957, 0.5: 0.8274, 0.75: 0.8324, 1.0: 0.8473; still rising, so more training scenarios should help more than regularisation.

recommendation_for_the_owner: Keep v3-account-1.0.0 served. Do not promote the v3-account-1.1.0 artifact as it is: its stored threshold violates its own precision >= 0.5 rule on validation because of the isotonic tie, and at that threshold it flags more long-history ordinary accounts, victims and innocent counterparties than the champion at the ledger end.

On ranking at the ledger end the two are close on validation and cold (PR-AUC intervals overlap; at the champion's validation FPR the challenger's cold recall is slightly lower and its cold FPR lower, see the 'matched' analysis threshold), better on the demo ledger, and better calibrated (Brier, ECE). Its clear gain is on short histories and earlier snapshots (fpr_by_history_band_all_snapshots, fpr_by_as_of_day), which the champion never saw in training (ledger-end rows only) and where the champion flags about a third of negatives under 30 days of history.

Conditions for replacement: (1) threshold selection that keeps tied scores together (or selection on raw scores), chosen on validation only; (2) a promotion rule that also requires validation FPR on >= 90-day histories and the flag rates of victims and innocent counterparties to be no worse than the champion's; (3) because this report has now shown cold/demo results for the analysis thresholds, confirmation on a fresh ledger (new seed) that no choice has seen, scored once.

Worth testing next, on train/validation only: a feature set with graph features but without account-age features, and more training scenario instances (the learning curve has not flattened). The residual rise of FPR with history length should be tracked as its own validation metric.
